question: How did you measure this proxy honestly, and what could still make the numbers misleading?
answer_hinglish:
Maine pehle sawal tay kiya ('proxy kitna cost karta hai?'), phir ek runner (`bench/run.mjs`) banaya jo har experiment ke raw JSON files save karta hai, aur README ki tables un files se script se generate hoti hain: koi number haath se type nahi hua. Har load row 3 runs ka median hai (min-max bhi dikhaya), kyunki ek hi run noise ho sakti hai. Har result ke saath date, Node version, machine, commit aur CPU steal (hypervisor ne doosre tenants ko kitna time diya) save hota hai: is run mein steal 0.2 percent tha, toh neighbours ka shor kam tha.

Phir bhi numbers bhramak ho sakte hain, aur maine yeh README mein likha hai: load generator, proxy aur upstream teeno ek hi 2-core machine par chale, loopback par. Isliye absolute numbers production capacity nahi hain, sirf rows ki aapas mein tulna valid hai. Do machines, asli network, ya internet se client measure nahi hua. Free-tier VM ke cores ki speed time ke saath badal sakti hai. Aur autocannon khud CPU leta hai.

Interview mein bolo: kaun sa sawal, kaun sa setup, kitni baar, kya record kiya, aur kya NAHI measure kiya. Yeh teeno baatein 'maine benchmark kiya' se kaafi zyada bharosa deti hain.
why_needed: Performance numbers tabhi kaam ke hain jab pata ho ki woh kaise bane aur kis cheez par laagu hote hain.
real_world_analogy: Doctor ek reading par faisla nahi karta: kai reading, normal range, aur patient ki halat dekhta hai.
how_it_works: Raw data pehle, summary baad mein, aur summary script se. Median ke saath spread. Environment record.
disadvantages: Ek hi machine par sab kuch
Sirf 3 runs, free-tier VM ki speed badal sakti hai
common_mistakes: Ek run ka best number batana
Machine aur setup likhe bina numbers dena
follow_up_questions: Confidence interval kaise nikaloge?
Coordinated omission kya hota hai?

question: What does the proxy cost compared with calling the upstream directly?
answer_hinglish:
E1 mein same upstream ko do tareeke se maara: seedha, aur proxy ke through (32 connections, chhote responses, 15 second x 3 runs). Direct: 14953 req/s median, p50 2 ms. Proxy ke through: 3586 req/s (min-max 3251 - 3608), p50 8 ms, p99 14 ms. Yani proxy ke saath lagbhag 24 percent request rate mila, aur median latency 2 se 8 ms hui. Errors zero rahe.

Yeh 'negligible' nahi hai, aur maine pehle jo bhi andaza lagaya tha usse zyada hai. Wajah: har request ko proxy ko parse karna padta hai, naya upstream request banana, headers copy, response wapas likhna: ek HTTP hop ka kaam do baar. Aur sab ek JavaScript thread par: Node ek core use karta hai. Is run mein load generator, proxy aur upstream teeno 2 cores baant rahe the, isliye numbers machine ke saath bandhe hain.

Dhyan: yeh comparison hai, capacity nahi. Per-process CPU maine alag se measure nahi kiya, toh 'proxy ne ek poora core saturate kiya' ek anumaan hai. Interview mein yeh bolna sahi: proxy ke saath latency aur throughput ka real price hota hai; usse sahi jagah (TLS, balancing, failover) ke liye chukate hain.
why_needed: Proxy ka asli cost jaan ke use karna ya na karna tay karna.
real_world_analogy: Beech ka agent: har parcel ko khol ke dobara pack karta hai, toh seedha bhejne se thoda dheema hi hoga.
how_it_works: Do HTTP parsers aur do TCP connections per request, ek thread par.
code_example:
| target | req/s (median) | p50 ms | p99 ms |
| direct | 14953 | 2 | 4 |
| proxy  | 3586 | 8 | 14 |
common_mistakes: 'Proxy negligible overhead' bolna
Is number ko production capacity maan lena
follow_up_questions: Is overhead ko kaise kam karoge?
Multiple processes se throughput kitna badhega? (measure nahi kiya)

question: What did per-request logging cost, and what would you do about it?
answer_hinglish:
E1 ki teesri row mein proxy ko `REQUEST_LOG=false` ke saath chalaya (per-request JSON line band, baaki sab same). Result: 4044 req/s (min-max 4026 - 4105) bamukabil 3586 req/s (min-max 3251 - 3608) jab logging on thi. Yani 12.8 percent zyada throughput. Dono ke min-max ranges overlap nahi karte, toh yeh noise nahi lagta.

Matlab har request par ek `console.log(JSON.stringify(...))` ka ek samay ka cost hai jo is rate par dikhta hai. Yahi sabak P01 mein bhi mila tha: synchronous logging event loop ko block karti hai. Yahan stdout ek pipe tha (runner ke paas); journald ke saath cost alag ho sakta hai, maine woh measure nahi kiya.

Options: (1) logging default on rakhna kyunki log hi failures ko explain karta hai (maine yeh chuna). (2) Switch dena (`REQUEST_LOG=false`): maine diya. (3) Sampling: sirf errors aur slow requests log karna. (4) Async buffered logger (P01 ka QueueHandler jaisa). (5) Metrics counters + sirf failures ka log. Maine 3 aur 4 implement nahi kiye. Interview mein: measure karo, phir decide karo; yahan data ne kaha ki cost real hai (~12.8 percent), lekin default nahi badla.
why_needed: Observability ka cost jaan ke trade-off karna.
real_world_analogy: CCTV har kamre mein: suraksha behtar par bijli aur storage ka kharcha.
how_it_works: Har request par ek synchronous write. Cost rate ke saath badhta hai.
code_example: log: process.env.REQUEST_LOG === "false" ? undefined : (entry) => console.log(JSON.stringify(entry)),
advantages: Failures explain karne ke liye default on
disadvantages: Sampling aur async logger nahi hain
journald ke saath cost measure nahi kiya
common_mistakes: Logging ko 'free' maanna
Bina measure kiye logging band kar dena
follow_up_questions: Async logger kaise banaoge?
Sampling ki policy kya hogi?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Per-request logs debugging ke liye anmol hain par rate ke saath cost badhta hai. Metrics (counters, histograms) sasti hain; logs sirf anomalies ke liye rakhna ek aam balance hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Slow log sink (journald ya disk full) event loop ko block kar sakta hai aur poora proxy slow ho jata hai: P01 jaisa bug.
advanced.alternatives: Sampling, async buffered logger, binary logging, metrics only with error logs.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x rate par logging cost proportional badhta hai; sampling ya async zaroori. 100x par logs ko proxy ke bahar (sidecar ya agent) bhejna.
advanced.production_improvements: Async logger, sampling, per-request metrics endpoint, aur journald/pipe ke saath cost measurement.

question: What did the round-robin vs least-connections measurement show, and what did it NOT show?
answer_hinglish:
E2 mein do upstreams: ek turant jawab deta hai, doosra 40 ms extra leta hai. 32 connections, 15 second x 3 runs har strategy ke liye. Round-robin: 1524 req/s, p50 15 ms, slow upstream ko 50% traffic. Least-connections: 3400 req/s, p50 6 ms, slow ko sirf 7.3% traffic. Throughput lagbhag 2.2 guna aur median latency aadhe se bhi kam.

Kyun: least-connections slow upstream ki requests ko 'busy' dekhta hai (zyada der active rehti hain), toh naye requests tez upstream ko jaate hain. Round-robin har doosri request slow ko deta hai, aur woh clients ko slow banata hai (kyunki 32 connections mein se aadhe slow par atke rehte hain).

Kya NAHI dikha: tail (p99) behtar nahi hua: 46 ms (round-robin) vs 49 ms (least-connections). Wajah: jo requests slow upstream tak pahunchi, woh ab bhi 40 ms leti hain. Least-connections ne zyada requests ko slow se bachaya, lekin jo gayi unko nahi bachaya. Yeh bhi nahi pata chala ki kai servers, alag load shapes ya asli network par kya hoga. Toh claim: 'is workload par, is machine par, least-connections ne throughput aur median sudhara, tail nahi'.
why_needed: Strategy ka asli asar jaan ke recommendation dena.
real_world_analogy: Do cashier, ek dheema: line ko tez waale ki taraf bhejne se average wait ghatta hai, par jo dheeme ke paas phans gaya uska wait wahi rahta hai.
how_it_works: Active count slow upstream par jama hota hai, aur least-connections usse door rakhta hai.
code_example:
| strategy | req/s | p50 ms | p99 ms | slow share |
| round-robin | 1524 | 15 | 46 | 50% |
| least-connections | 3400 | 6 | 49 | 7.3% |
common_mistakes: Sirf average dekhna aur tail ignore karna
Result ko har workload par laagu karna
follow_up_questions: Tail latency ko kaise sudharoge?
Hedged requests yahan kaise madad karenge?

question: What happened when an upstream was killed under load, with and without retries?
answer_hinglish:
E3 mein 2 upstreams, round-robin, 32 connections, 14 second ka run; 5 second par ek upstream ko SIGKILL (bina warning). 3 runs har configuration. Retries band: 16 (9 - 21) bad requests (median, min-max), aakhri bad request kill ke 17 ms ke andar khatam. Retries 1: 0 (0 - 0): kisi run mein client tak koi failure nahi pahuncha, aur kill ke baad 7 requests (median) retry se bachi.

Passive ejection ne maut ko kill ke lagbhag 8 ms mein pakad liya, kyunki 32 busy connections ek saath failures dete hain aur 3 lagatar failures turant ho jaate hain. Phir upstream rotation se bahar, aur traffic doosre par.

Dhyan: 'bad' ginti proxy ke log se hai (5xx ya beech mein kata body). Yeh SIGKILL ka case hai: connection turant reset hota hai. Black hole (packets silently drop) ka case alag hai (E5) aur dheema hota hai. Aur yeh 2 upstreams ka test hai: ek bacha hua server poora load le sakta tha. Agar doosra bhi bharaa hota toh result alag hota.
why_needed: Failover ka asli asar numbers mein jaanna.
real_world_analogy: Ek lift kharab hui: log doosri lift par jaate hain; jo andar thhe unko bahar nikalna padta hai, par naye log seedha doosri par.
how_it_works: Connection reset par attempt fail, retry doosre target par, aur 3 lagatar failures par ejection.
code_example:
retries 0: 16 (9 - 21) bad, last bad 17 ms after the kill
retries 1: 0 (0 - 0) bad, 7 requests saved by retry
advantages: Retries ne client ko failures se bachaya
disadvantages: Sirf abrupt kill: black hole alag
Do upstreams, bacha hua server poora load le sakta tha
common_mistakes: Kill ko hi sabse bura failure maanna
'bad' ki definition na batana
follow_up_questions: Slow failure par kya hota hai?
Retry ke saath upstream par extra load kitna padta hai?

question: Active health checks added nothing in the kill experiment. Does that mean they are useless?
answer_hinglish:
E3 mein 'active checks every 1s' wali rows ka result passive-only jaisa hi raha: retries 0 ke saath 18 (9 - 18) bad (passive-only: 16 (9 - 21)), retries 1 ke saath 0 dono mein. Down event bhi lagbhag 10 ms par aaya, jo passive ejection ka event hai: active probe 1 second interval aur 2 failures ke saath kam az kam 1 se 2 second leta, toh passive ne pehle pakda. Yani is scenario mein active ka koi faayda nahi dikha.

Lekin 'useless' nahi: yeh scenario wahi hai jahan passive sabse tez hota hai (bahut traffic, turant reset). Active checks tab kaam aate hain jab (1) kisi upstream par traffic hi nahi aa raha (passive ko failures milte hi nahi), (2) recovery pata karni ho: ejected server ke wapas aane ka pata sirf trial request se chalta hai ya probe se, (3) failure slow ho (hang, black hole) aur har request ko timeout jhelna pade, probe pehle bata deta hai.

Service test mein recovery active check se hi hui: upstream restart ke baad '2 health checks passed' event aaya. Is project ne in teeno cases ko alag alag isolate karke measure nahi kiya: yeh limitation hai. Ek achha agla experiment: ek upstream ko idle rakho aur band karo, dekho kitni der mein pata chalta hai.
why_needed: Ek measurement result ko sahi context mein padhna.
real_world_analogy: Smoke alarm ghar mein sabse tez tab bajta hai jab aag sirf ek kamre mein hoti hai; par raat ko sab so rahe hon toh wahi akela guard hai.
how_it_works: Passive: failures par depend. Active: timer par. Jis scenario mein failures bahut hain, passive jeetta hai.
disadvantages: Idle upstream wala case measure nahi hua
common_mistakes: 'Active checks bekaar hain' kehna
Ek scenario se poori design par faisla
follow_up_questions: Idle upstream wala experiment kaise design karoge?
Probe interval ka detection time par asar?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Active checks traffic se independent hote hain par extra load aur latency lagate hain. Passive free hai par failures par depend. Dono ek doosre ko cover karte hain.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Idle ya low-traffic upstream: passive blind. Black hole: har request ko connect timeout lagta hai, probe jaldi bata sakta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Sirf passive, sirf active, ya success-rate based outlier detection.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada traffic par passive aur bhi tez; low-traffic services par active zaroori.
advanced.production_improvements: Idle-upstream experiment, probe interval tuning, aur detection time ka metric.

question: What did the connect timeout experiment against a real black hole show?
answer_hinglish:
E5 mein ek upstream ko firewall se 'black hole' banaya: uske SYN packets silently drop ho rahe the (loopback par iptables DROP). Upstream order [dead, live], round-robin, retries 1. Connect timeout 1000 ms par pehle teen GET 1020, 1005, 1006 ms mein 200 se khatam hue, har ek ne ConnectTimeoutError ke saath 2 attempts liye: pehla attempt dead par poora timeout wait kiya, phir retry live par. Chauthi request se dead upstream eject ho chuka tha (3 lagatar failures), aur requests 4 ms mein aane lagi. Timeout 3000 ms par wahi pattern: 3018, 3007, 3006 ms, phir 3 ms.

Seekha: black hole mein har request ko poora connect timeout bharna padta hai jab tak upstream eject na ho. Ejection ke liye 3 failures chahiye, toh teen users ne poora timeout bhugta. Isliye same data-centre ke upstreams ke liye CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS ko 500 se 1000 ke aaspaas rakhna behtar (default 3000 safe general value hai). Chhota timeout nuksan: asli slow network par galat failures.

POST ko 504 mila 1118 ms baad, 1 attempt ke saath: retry nahi hua (sahi, kyunki POST safe nahi). Honest limit: yeh sirf loopback par hua; asli network par RTT aur packet loss alag hote.
why_needed: Black hole failures ke asli cost ko samajhna, kyunki yeh 'refused' se bahut zyada dheema hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Aap bell bajate ho aur koi darwaza nahi kholta: intezaar kitna karna hai, yeh aapka faisla hai.
how_it_works: SYN drop hone par kernel retransmit karta hai, jawab nahi aata. Humara timer connect timeout par request ko destroy karta hai.
code_example: iptables -I OUTPUT -p tcp -d 127.0.0.1 --dport <port> -j DROP   # every rule is removed in a finally block plus a 120 s watchdog
advantages: Real black hole par verify hua
Retry aur ejection ka combined asar dikha
disadvantages: Ejection tak teen users ne poora timeout bhugta
common_mistakes: Connect timeout ko request timeout ke barabar rakhna
Black hole test mein rule hatana bhool jana
follow_up_questions: Ejection ko tez kaise karoge?
Connect timeout ko RTT se kaise tune karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Chhota connect timeout jaldi failover deta hai par slow networks par galat positives. Lamba timeout safe par har user ko bhugatna.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Network partition: sab connects hang. Half-open firewall: kuch ports drop, kuch accept.
advanced.alternatives: Probe-based jaldi detection, parallel connects (happy eyeballs), per-upstream adaptive timeout.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada upstreams par black hole wala server bhi zyada requests jhelta jab tak eject na ho: ejection ki speed important.
advanced.production_improvements: Connect timeout RTT ke hisaab se, probe se pehle detection, aur black-hole test ko do-host mode mein.

question: A closed port can fail in three different ways. Which did you measure, and which not?
answer_hinglish:
Closed port par client ko teen alag cheezein mil sakti hain. (1) ECONNREFUSED: kernel turant RST bhejta hai. Same host par aise hi hota hai: E6 mein Linux par proxy ne `ECONNREFUSED` record kiya aur client ko 502 mila. (2) EHOSTUNREACH ('No route to host'): firewall ne REJECT rule ke saath ICMP 'host prohibited' bheja. (3) Timeout: firewall ne chup chaap DROP kiya (black hole), E5.

Maine Oracle servers ki iptables dekhi: INPUT chain sirf 22, 80, 443 accept karti hai aur baaki par `REJECT --reject-with icmp-host-prohibited`. Matlab doosre host se band port par jaane par client ko EHOSTUNREACH milna chahiye, ECONNREFUSED nahi. Humari retry list mein EHOSTUNREACH hai, lekin yeh MEASURE NAHI hua: sab experiments ek host par chale.

Yeh isliye zaroori: agar retry list mein sirf ECONNREFUSED hota, toh production mein firewall ke peeche band port par retry kaam nahi karta. Interview mein: error codes ko list se jodna kaafi nahi, har ek ko asli failure se verify karna padta hai. Do-host experiment is gap ko band karega, lekin usse Oracle ki shared security list badalni padti, jo maine abhi nahi ki.
why_needed: Alag network failures ke alag error codes samajhna.
real_world_analogy: Band dukaan: board par 'band hai' (refused), 'aap yahan allowed nahi' (host prohibited), ya koi jawab hi nahi (timeout).
how_it_works: Kernel ya firewall ka jawab client ke error code mein badal jata hai: ECONNREFUSED, EHOSTUNREACH, ya connect timeout.
code_example: const RETRYABLE_CODES = new Set(["ECONNREFUSED", "ECONNRESET", "EPIPE", "EHOSTUNREACH", "ENETUNREACH", "EAI_AGAIN", "ENOTFOUND"]);
advantages: Error list asli firewall ko dekh ke judi
common_mistakes: Sirf ECONNREFUSED ko retry karna
Same-host test se cross-host behaviour maan lena
follow_up_questions: Do-host experiment kaise karoge?
ICMP block ho toh kya dikhega?

question: You said the proxy streams bodies. Did memory actually stay flat for a 1 GiB response?
answer_hinglish:
E7 mein upstream ne 1 GiB (1073741824 bytes) ki file stream ki aur proxy ke through ek client ne usko consume karke phek diya. Poora size aaya (complete: yes), 2.7 second mein. Proxy ka RSS (resident memory) idle par 41.1 MiB tha aur transfer ke dauran max 81.7 MiB: yani 40.6 MiB ka izafa, 1024 MiB ka nahi. Upstream ka max 48.8 MiB.

Isse pata chalta hai ki proxy body ko poori tarah buffer nahi karta (warna 1 GiB badhta). Lekin 'bilkul flat' bolna galat hoga: thoda badha aur phir ruk gaya. Aam wajah: Node ke stream buffers aur garbage collector ke chale bina memory wapas nahi aati; ek chhota fixed 'working set' (pipe ke buffers, ek-do chunks) hota hai.

Pehle meri claim 'memory flat rehti hai' ek design property thi, measure nahi hui thi: ab measure hui aur thodi badli hui bhasha ke saath README mein likhi hai. Aur do cheezein measure nahi hui: bada UPLOAD proxy ke through, aur kai bade transfers ek saath (har ek apna working set lega). Interview mein: 'bounded, aur measured, sirf download ke liye'.
why_needed: Design claim ko measurement se pakka karna.
real_world_analogy: Paani ki pipe: tanki nahi bharti, lekin pipe ke andar thoda paani hamesha rehta hai.
how_it_works: pipe() ke saath back-pressure: source tabhi padhta hai jab destination likh sake. Memory sirf chunks ke buffers ki.
in_this_project: bench/scenarios.mjs::e7 (RSS ko /proc se 200 ms par sample karta hai); src/proxy.ts pipe.
code_example: idle 41.1 MiB -> max 81.7 MiB while 1024 MiB went through (40.6 MiB growth)
disadvantages: Upload aur concurrent transfers measure nahi hue
common_mistakes: 'Flat' bolna jab thoda badha ho
Sirf design se claim karna
follow_up_questions: Concurrent bade transfers par memory kitni hogi?
Upload ke liye same test kaise karoge?

question: What did the 30-minute soak prove, and what could it not prove?
answer_hinglish:
E8 mein 16 concurrent clients ne 1800 second tak mix traffic bheja: 70 percent GET, 10 percent slow GET, 10 percent aise GET jinhe client 1 se 30 ms mein abort kar deta, 10 percent POST. Teen upstreams, ek mein 5 percent connection resets. Least-connections, retries 1, active health checks. Proxy ne 2851253 requests log kiye.

Jo prove hua: kaam rukne ke baad har upstream ki active count 0, 0, 0 thi, yani 28 lakh se zyada requests, aborts aur failures ke baad bhi koi lease leak nahi hui. Proxy memory shuru mein 83.4 MiB se badhke lagbhag 91.1 MiB par theher gayi (10 minute ke baad plateau). Process zinda raha 164 health up/down events ke beech. 23819 requests retry hui, aur proxy ne 26532 ECONNRESET dekhe jo flaky upstream ki wajah se the. POST ko flaky par retry nahi mila, toh kuch 502 gaye, jo expected hai.

Jo prove NAHI ho sakta: plateau ek chhoti leak ko rule out nahi karta, sirf badi leak ko. Machine ~89 percent busy thi (zyadatar load generator), toh yeh capacity ka test nahi, correctness ka hai. Aur sab loopback par. 30 minute 24 ghante nahi hote.
why_needed: Long-running correctness (leaks, drift) ko dekhna jo chhote tests nahi pakadte.
real_world_analogy: Gaadi ko ek hafte ki city driving: chhoti test drive mein jo nahi dikhta woh dikhta hai, par factory test ke barabar nahi.
how_it_works: Stats line har 5 second active counts dikhati hai; aakhri line se leak check hota hai.
code_example: final active counts: [0, 0, 0]   (after 2851253 requests)
disadvantages: Plateau chhoti leak ko rule out nahi karta
common_mistakes: Soak ko capacity test samajhna
Memory plateau ko 'no leak' ka proof maan lena
follow_up_questions: 24 ghante ka soak kaise design karoge?
Memory leak ko heap snapshot se kaise dhoondhoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Lamba soak zyada confidence deta hai par CI mein nahi chal sakta; release se pehle ek baar chalana aur chhote versions CI mein rakhna ek balance hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Slow memory leak (kuch KB per hazaar requests) 30 minute mein nahi dikhegi. Counter leak turant dikhti hai (active nonzero).
advanced.alternatives: Heap snapshots, --trace-gc, long soak with production-like traffic replay.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada traffic par leak jaldi dikhti hai; low-traffic par der.
advanced.production_improvements: 24 ghante ka soak, heap growth alert, aur active gauge ko metrics mein.

question: Did you manage to reproduce the stale keep-alive reset? What did it depend on?
answer_hinglish:
Pehli koshish mein nahi: Node upstream (1 second se kam keep-alive timeout) ke saath 300 requests mein koi reset nahi dikha, na retries 0 par na 1 par. Maine soch ke dekha ki Node ka server har response mein `Keep-Alive: timeout=N` hint bhejta hai, aur Node ka http client us hint ko use karke connection reuse se pehle hi bacha leta hoga. Isliye ek 'raw' upstream banaya: seedha TCP par likha HTTP/1.1 server jo koi Keep-Alive hint nahi bhejta aur 200 ms idle ke baad connection band kar deta hai.

Raw upstream ke saath race dikhi. Retries 0: 300 mein se {"200":299,"502":1} (client ne dekha), proxy ne {"ECONNRESET":1} dekha. Retries 1: client ne {"200":300} dekha, proxy ne {"ECONNRESET":2} ECONNRESET dekhe aur 2 requests retry hui, yani retry ne reset ko client se chhupa liya (log mein `error` set aur `attempts` 2).

Do caveats. (1) Hint wali baat meri hypothesis hai: dono servers ke result alag the, par maine Node ke client ke source ya alag test se yeh confirm nahi kiya. (2) Race rare hai (300 mein 1 ya 2), toh yeh production error rate nahi batata, sirf yeh ki failure real hai aur retry usse hide karta hai. Node upstream ke saath bhi race ka darr bana rehta hai agar hint na bheje ya proxies beech mein ho.
why_needed: Ek mushkil race ko asli roop mein reproduce karna, aur uski shartein samajhna.
real_world_analogy: Do darwaazay band hone se pehle ek ghanti ka warning (hint) dete hain ya nahi: warning milne par aap pehle se bahar nikal jaate ho.
how_it_works: Server ne idle connection close ki usi pal client ne us par request likh di: request kho gayi, ECONNRESET. Retry naya connection kholta hai.
in_this_project: bench/upstream.mjs RAW mode; bench/scenarios.mjs::e4; src/proxy.ts retry.
code_example:
// raw upstream: closes idle connections with no warning and sends no Keep-Alive header
socket.setTimeout(idleMs, () => socket.destroy());
advantages: Race asli roop mein reproduce hui
disadvantages: Rare race: rate production ka nahi
common_mistakes: Pehli failed reproduction par 'race hai hi nahi' maan lena
Test upstream ko asli upstream jaisa maan lena
follow_up_questions: Agent ka idle timeout upstream se chhota kaise rakhoge?
Is race ko POST ke liye kaise handle karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Proactive: agent ka free-socket timeout upstream se kam. Reactive: retry. Dono saath best; sirf retry POST ko cover nahi karta.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Reset ke baad retry bhi fail: 502. POST par reset: 502, kyunki retry nahi.
advanced.alternatives: Keep-alive band karna (slow), HTTP/2, undici pool ka reconnect.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada traffic par race ki baar-baar hit; reset ka alag counter chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: Agent free-socket timeout, ECONNRESET ka alag metric, idempotency key POST ke liye.

question: Measuring graceful shutdown found a real defect. What was it, how did you find it, and how was it fixed?
answer_hinglish:
E9: 10 requests, har ek 2 second ki, flight mein; 0.5 second par SIGTERM. Kaam SIGTERM ke lagbhag 1500 ms baad khatam hona chahiye. Result (fix se pehle): sab 10 requests 200 se complete hui, exit code 0, lekin process SIGTERM ke 4540 ms baad exit hua: kaam khatam hone ke baad lagbhag 3040 ms extra. Linux par asli CLI test bhi 3840 ms leta tha jab ki request ~700 ms ki thi.

Wajah: `server.close()` sirf unhi connections ko band karta hai jo us pal idle hon. Jo connection SIGTERM ke waqt busy tha, woh response ke baad idle keep-alive ban jata hai, aur server.close() client ke hang-up ka intezaar karta rehta hai (seconds). Meri purani shutdown function `closeIdleConnections()` ek hi baar bulati thi: busy connection par asar nahi.

Fix: `gracefulShutdown()` (src/shutdown.ts) draining ke dauran har 100 ms par `closeIdleConnections()` chalata hai, aur 10 second ke baad 'forced' report karta hai. Fix ke baad: exit 1611 ms par (kaam ke upar ~111 ms), 10 mein se 10 ab bhi 200. Test: in-process (har OS par) aur asli CLI par SIGTERM ke saath (Linux). Pehle testing se hi 'shutdown ka koi test nahi' limitation pakdi gayi thi; measurement ne bug dikhaya.
why_needed: Deploy ke waqt exit time aur dropped requests production ko seedha chhute hain.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan band karte waqt jo grahak andar bill bana raha hai usko jaane do, lekin uske jaate hi shutter girao; uske ruke rehne ka intezaar mat karo.
how_it_works: server.close() accept band karta hai; idle connections ko khud sweep karna padta hai jab tak active requests khatam na ho.
disadvantages: Draining signal load balancer ko nahi jata (alag kaam)
common_mistakes: Ek baar closeIdleConnections() bulana kaafi samajhna
Shutdown ko sirf code padh ke 'theek' maan lena
follow_up_questions: Load balancer ko drain ka signal kaise doge?
Force-exit timer kitna rakhoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Sweep interval chhota = jaldi exit par thoda CPU; bada = der. 100 ms ek aaram wala balance. Force timer in-flight requests ki max duration se bada rakhna.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Request jo kabhi khatam na ho: 10 second ke baad forced exit (code 1). Do SIGTERM: ek hi shutdown (guard).
advanced.alternatives: Connection: close header SIGTERM ke baad ke responses par, ya server.close ke baad har response par 'Connection: close'.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada connections par sweep ka cost chhota hi hai; asli kaam load balancer se pehle drain karna.
advanced.production_improvements: Readiness endpoint jo SIGTERM par fail ho, Kubernetes jaisa preStop, aur shutdown time ka metric.

question: How do you prove that a regression test really catches the bug it is written for?
answer_hinglish:
Test ko pehle fail hote hue dekho. Shutdown fix ke liye maine yeh kiya: `gracefulShutdown()` ki sweep line (`setInterval(... closeIdleConnections ...)`) hata ke test chalaye. Do tests fail hue (5 second ka timeout: bilkul purani behaviour jaisa, jahan server keep-alive timeout tak ruka rehta), aur line wapas lagane par chaaron pass hue (sabse lamba test lagbhag 350 ms). Agar test ko fail hote hue na dekha jaye, toh woh sirf 'green' hone ka vaada hai, bug pakadne ka nahi.

Yehi tareeka maine poore project mein apnaya (mutation check): ek behaviour jaan-boojh ke tod ke dekha ki uska test red hota hai. Isse do asli gaps mile: (1) body-less POST ka retry kisi test se nahi pakda gaya tha kyunki purana POST test body ke saath tha aur body wali request waise bhi replayable nahi thi; (2) ek helper (`deadPort`) race wala tha, jiski wajah se files ek ek karke chalti hain.

Dhyan: mutation manual hai, automated nahi (Stryker jaisa tool nahi). Isliye coverage poora nahi: sirf wahi behaviours tode jinke baare mein socha. Aur har mutation ke baad code ko wapas restore karna aur poora suite dobara chalana zaroori hai, warna tooti cheez commit ho sakti hai.
why_needed: Tests par bharosa tabhi hota hai jab pata ho ki woh fail kar sakte hain.
real_world_analogy: Smoke detector ko test button se bajake dekhna: bina dekhe usko 'working' maan lena khatarnak hai.
how_it_works: Behaviour todo, test chalao, red dekho, restore karo, green dekho.
in_this_project: test/graceful.test.ts; test/resilience.test.ts; README 'Checked by breaking the code' notes.
code_example:
// old behaviour: remove the sweep line, then the test must time out
// sweep = setInterval(() => server.closeIdleConnections(), sweepMs);
common_mistakes: Test ko kabhi fail hote hue na dekhna
Mutation ke baad restore na karna
follow_up_questions: Mutation testing tool kaise kaam karta hai?
Kitna mutation score kaafi hai?

question: Walk through the systemd unit for the proxy and explain each hardening choice.
answer_hinglish:
Unit file `deploy/reverse-proxy.service` mein: `User=reverse-proxy` (ek system user jo login nahi kar sakta aur kuch own nahi karta), `EnvironmentFile=/etc/reverse-proxy.env` (settings code se alag), `ExecStart` Node ka full path (PATH par depend nahi), `Restart=on-failure` aur `RestartSec=2` (crash par wapas), `KillSignal=SIGTERM` aur `TimeoutStopSec=15`: proxy ka apna force-exit 10 second par hai, toh systemd ko usse zyada rukna chahiye warna graceful shutdown beech mein SIGKILL ho jata.

Hardening: `NoNewPrivileges=true` (privilege badhne se rokta hai), `ProtectSystem=strict` (poora filesystem read-only), `ProtectHome=true` (home folders invisible), `PrivateTmp`, `PrivateDevices`, `ProtectKernelTunables/Modules`, `ProtectControlGroups`, `RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET AF_INET6 AF_UNIX` (sirf network aur unix sockets), `RestrictNamespaces`, `LockPersonality`, aur `MemoryMax=256M` (runaway memory ko cap).

Result: `systemd-analyze security` ne exposure level 5.8 MEDIUM diya. Yani abhi bhi sudhar ki gunjaish hai (jaise SystemCallFilter, CapabilityBoundingSet jaisi settings maine nahi lagayi). Maine isse 'fully locked down' nahi bola. Aur unit ko asli server par chala ke dekha: service reverse-proxy user ke taur par chali, sirf 127.0.0.1:8080 par suni, aur `systemctl stop` 0.03 second mein 'Result=success' ke saath ruka.
why_needed: Service ko least-privilege par chalana aur restart/stop sahi rakhna.
real_world_analogy: Kaarigar ko sirf uski workshop ki chaabi dena, poori building ki nahi.
how_it_works: systemd sandboxing options kernel features (namespaces, seccomp-lite, mount options) se laagu hote hain.
code_example:
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=true
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET AF_INET6 AF_UNIX
MemoryMax=256M
TimeoutStopSec=15
common_mistakes: Root se service chalana
TimeoutStopSec ko force-exit se chhota rakhna
follow_up_questions: SystemCallFilter kaise lagate hain?
Exposure score ko aur kaise girayenge?

question: Why was everything kept on loopback and non-public, and how were the risky experiment steps made safe?
answer_hinglish:
Stage 4 ke liye maine koi naya port nahi kholna chaha: proxy `127.0.0.1` par sunta hai aur A2 ki security list ya Oracle ka koi network rule nahi badla. Wajah: (1) bina zaroorat ke public exposure ek attack surface hai, (2) shared Oracle security list badalna doosre server (jahan ek aur application chal rahi hai) ko bhi chhoo sakta hai, aur (3) is stage ka maqsad measurement tha, public service nahi. Test: service ke baad bahar se port 8080 par jaane par jawab nahi mila.

Jo steps risky the, unke liye guard rakhe. E5 mein iptables DROP rule lagana padta hai: script usse `finally` mein hatati hai, aur ek alag detached watchdog 120 second baad bhi hatata hai chahe script mar jaye; reboot bhi rule saaf kar deta hai (rules save nahi hue). Rule sirf ek loopback port ke liye, sab traffic ke liye nahi, taaki SSH lockout ka khatra na ho. Har experiment ke baad check kiya ki `iptables -S OUTPUT | grep DROP` khali hai.

Node install ke liye checksum verify kiya (SHA-256 SHASUMS file se: 'OK'). Dhyan: yeh signature verify nahi hai: yahi site se checksum hai. Aur `npm ci` lockfile ke integrity hashes par chalta hai. Repo mein koi IP, key ya token nahi gaya (reference results scan ki: sirf loopback addresses).
why_needed: Test infrastructure bhi attack surface aur outage ka karan ban sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Chemistry lab: experiment se pehle fire blanket aur emergency shower ki jagah dekh lo.
how_it_works: Narrow rule + automatic cleanup + verification har baar.
code_example:
const watchdog = spawn("sh", ["-c", `sleep 120; sudo -n iptables -D ${rule.join(" ")} 2>/dev/null`], { detached: true, stdio: "ignore" });
// ... and in finally: ipt("-D", ...rule)
advantages: Risky rule ke liye do safety nets
common_mistakes: Test ke liye security list kholna
Rule hatane ka koi fallback na rakhna
follow_up_questions: GPG signature kaise verify karte hain?
Test rule ko aur kaise sandbox karoge (network namespace)?

question: On the real service, what did stopping and restarting the upstream show?
answer_hinglish:
systemd service ke saath ek demo upstream chalaya aur use rok diya. Pehli do requests ko 502 mila, teesri ko 503. Yeh isliye: har GET 2 attempts leta hai (1 + 1 retry, usi akele upstream par), aur har attempt ek failure ginta hai, toh 3 lagatar failures do requests mein poore ho gaye. Teesri request par upstream ejected tha, toh seedha 503 'No Healthy Upstream' bina upstream ko chhue.

12 second baad bhi 503 aur `Retry-After: 1` mila, aur journal mein do health events the: pehla `ejected for 10000 ms after 3 consecutive failures` (passive), doosra `2 health checks failed` (active). Upstream wapas start karne par 12 second ke andar request dobara 200 deti thi, aur journal mein `2 health checks passed` aaya: recovery apne aap hui, kisi ne proxy ko chhua nahi.

Aur `systemctl stop reverse-proxy` 0.03 second mein 'Result=success' (exit code 0) ke saath ruka, kyunki us waqt koi request in-flight nahi thi. Yeh sab ek hi demo upstream par hua, toh 'failover' nahi dikha (koi doosra server nahi tha): dikha ki failure detect hota hai, 503 sahi bhasha mein aata hai, aur recovery automatic hai. Do upstream ke saath failover E3 mein dikha.
why_needed: Service ke asli behaviour ko end to end dekhna.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan ka maal khatam: board 'abhi nahi hai, thodi der baad aana' (503 + Retry-After), maal aate hi dukaan khud khul gayi.
how_it_works: Passive ejection pehle, active checks baad mein, recovery sirf active ya trial se.
code_example:
request 1: 502   request 2: 502   request 3: 503
journal: ejected for 10000 ms after 3 consecutive failures / 2 health checks failed / 2 health checks passed
advantages: Logs se samajh aaya kya hua
disadvantages: Ek hi upstream: failover nahi dikha
common_mistakes: Retry attempts ko ek failure ginna (yahan har attempt gini jati hai)
503 ko 502 se alag na samajhna
follow_up_questions: Retry attempts ko ek hi failure kaise ginoge?
Recovery time kaise tune karoge?

question: Your first local numbers looked terrible (about 40 ms latency, a tenth of the throughput). What was going on?
answer_hinglish:
Windows PC par ek chhota 3 second ka dry run chalaya aur proxy ke through p50 lagbhag 40 ms aur throughput direct ka dasvaan hissa dikha. 40 ms ek jaana-pehchana number hai (Nagle aur delayed-ACK ka asar), toh pehle wahi shak hua. Lekin maine seedha anuman par kuch badla nahi; ek-ek cheez alag ki.

Pehli jaanch: 1 connection par direct bhi 15 ms p50 de raha tha. Yeh Windows ka timer resolution tha (~15 ms ka clock tick): meri test upstream har request par `setTimeout(..., 0)` laga rahi thi, aur Windows par 0 ms timer bhi tick tak ruk jata hai. Fix: delay 0 ho toh seedha jawab do. Yeh mere test tool ka bug tha, proxy ka nahi. Doosri jaanch: logging on/off compare ki; PC par numbers itne uchhalte the (413 se 2233 req/s ek hi config par) ki koi nateeja nahi nikla, kyunki machine par browser, IDE aur baaki processes chal rahe the.

Sabak: dev PC par benchmark mat chalao. Maine claim nahi kiya; ek quiet Linux server par 3 baar repeat kiya, steal record kiya, aur wahi numbers publish kiye. Wahan proxy lagbhag 24 percent request rate de raha tha aur p50 8 ms tha, 40 ms nahi: toh 40 ms Windows ka artifact tha.
why_needed: Measurement tool ke apne bugs aur environment noise ko pehchanna.
real_world_analogy: Raste par traffic jam mein speed test karna: gaadi nahi, raasta dheema hota hai.
how_it_works: Ek cheez badlo, dobara naapo. Noisy environment mein nateeje nikaalna band karo.
code_example: if (wait <= 0) return void res.end(name); // no timer: on Windows even setTimeout(0) waits for the ~15 ms clock tick
advantages: Noisy machine par claim nahi kiya
disadvantages: Pehle thodi der anuman par time gaya
common_mistakes: Pehle number ko proxy ka bug maan lena
Noisy machine ke numbers publish karna
follow_up_questions: Nagle algorithm aur delayed ACK ka interaction kya hai?
Timer resolution kaise check karte hain?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Dev PC par benchmark sasta aur turant hai par noisy; ek quiet dedicated server dheema setup par bharosemand. Pehle tool ko validate karo, phir system ko.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Tool ka bug (timer) proxy ke bug jaisa dikh sakta hai; noisy machine par galat conclusion; ek run par faisla.
advanced.alternatives: Dedicated benchmark machine, cgroups ya CPU pinning, container with fixed CPU quota, cloud benchmark runner.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bade systems mein benchmarks CI mein dedicated hardware par chalte hain aur regression thresholds ke saath.
advanced.production_improvements: CPU pinning (taskset), steal aur load record karna, aur har result ke saath environment save karna (jo ab hota hai).

question: Add a new experiment to the bench: which error does the proxy record for a closed port? Show the code of the existing one.
answer_hinglish:
Experiments `bench/scenarios.mjs` mein functions hain jo `{ title, note, columns, rows, raw }` return karte hain; `run.mjs` unhe chalata hai, `eN.json` save karta hai aur table banata hai. Naya experiment banane ke liye: ek function likho, `scenarios` object mein naam jodo, aur `node run.mjs <naam>` se chalao.

E6 sabse chhota udaharan hai: ek band port lo (`freePort()` kuch sunta nahi), proxy ko usi par point karo (`RETRIES=0`), ek GET bhejo, aur proxy ke log se `error` field padho. Linux par jawab `ECONNREFUSED` aur client ko status 502. Windows par bhi wahi aaya (local dry run mein).

Dhyan: `rows` raw se compute honi chahiye, haath se likhi nahi. Aur `note` mein honestly likho kya measure nahi hua (yahan: doosre host par band port). Agar experiment machine-specific hai (iptables, /proc), toh `{ skipped: "reason" }` return karo taaki doosri machine par saaf skip ho. Yeh tarika isliye achha hai ki run.mjs kisi ek experiment ke fail hone par baaki ko nahi rokta: har experiment try/catch mein chalta hai.
why_needed: Naye sawal ko jaldi measure kar sakna.
real_world_analogy: Lab mein ek naya test tube rack: tareeka wahi, sirf naya sample.
how_it_works: Scenario function -> run.mjs -> raw JSON -> generated tables.
advantages: Skipped aur failed alag dikhte hain
disadvantages: Har experiment ko khud cleanup likhna padta hai
common_mistakes: Rows haath se likhna
Machine-specific experiment ko bina skip ke chhodna

Result ko CI mein kaise regress-check karoge?

question: What would a two-host experiment add, and why was it not done?
answer_hinglish:
Ab tak sab ek host par (loopback) hua. Do-host mode mein proxy A2 par aur upstreams A1 par hote, private network ke upar. Isse yeh naya dikhta: (1) asli network latency aur uska retry/timeout par asar, (2) doosre host ke band port par `EHOSTUNREACH` ya REJECT ka asli behaviour (PROXY-083), (3) failover jab ek poori machine band ho, (4) load generator aur upstream ka CPU proxy se alag, toh proxy ki capacity zyada saaf dikhti.

Kyun nahi kiya: Oracle ki VCN security list mein A2 se A1 ke ports ke liye ek ingress rule chahiye (aur A1 ki iptables mein bhi), aur woh security list dono servers ke liye shared hai. A1 par doosri application chal rahi hai, isliye ek network rule badalna uske liye bhi asar rakhta. Maine plan mein likha tha ki yeh sirf tabhi karenge jab single-host se koi sawal khula reh jaye, aur sirf aapki explicit ijazat se. Do sawal khule hain (EHOSTUNREACH, asli RTT), lekin dono ke liye yeh risk abhi zaroori nahi laga.

Agar karna ho: rule sirf A2 ke private IP (/32) se, sirf do test ports ke liye, test ke baad hata do; A1 ki applications ko touch mat karo; aur har change ko reversible rakho. Alternative jisme koi shared rule nahi badalta: ek teesra chhota server ya A2 par containers ke beech virtual network (lekin woh asli RTT nahi dega).
why_needed: Measurement scope ke risk aur fayde ko tolna.
real_world_analogy: Pul ke load test ke liye doosre ilaake ka rasta band karna pad sakta hai: faayda aur nuksan dono tolo.
how_it_works: Shared infrastructure ke changes ka blast radius dekho, aur kam se kam rule se kaam chalao.
advantages: Risk aur faayde ka saaf hisaab
disadvantages: EHOSTUNREACH aur asli RTT abhi measure nahi hue
common_mistakes: Test ke liye shared security list ko bina soche badalna
Rule ko test ke baad na hatana
follow_up_questions: Network namespaces se do-host jaisa test kaise karoge?
Security list rule ko code (IaC) mein kaise rakhoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Zyada realistic test = zyada shared infrastructure chhuna. Chhote reversible steps aur explicit ijazat ek achha niyam hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Galat security list rule: A1 ke services ya SSH par asar ya, ulta, extra exposure.
advanced.alternatives: Teesra alag server, network namespaces, containers with bridge networks, cloud mein alag VCN.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Production-like testing ke liye ek alag staging network rakhna sahi hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Infrastructure-as-code se rule add/remove, aur staging VCN.

question: After measuring, which defaults did you change, and what evidence would make you change them?
answer_hinglish:
Koi default nahi badla: data ne unko contradict nahi kiya. `RETRIES=1`: E3 mein client tak koi failure nahi pahuncha aur E4 mein stale reset chhup gaya. `EJECT_AFTER=3`: load mein ejection milliseconds mein hua, aur kyunki har retry attempt bhi ek failure ginti hai, band upstream do requests mein eject ho jata hai (service test mein 502, 502, phir 503). `REQUEST_LOG` default on: logging ka cost real hai (E1) lekin log hi failures ko explain karta hai.

`CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS=3000` par data ne saaf price dikhaya (E5): black hole mein pehle teen requests ko poora 3 second bhugatna padta hai. Phir bhi default nahi badla kyunki sahi value environment par depend karti hai: same data-centre mein 500 se 1000 ms theek hai, lekin slow ya bhaari network par chhota timeout galat failures dega. README mein recommendation likhi hai, default nahi badla.

Kya data badal sakta hai: asli production traffic ke error rates, upstreams ka asli connect time (p99), aur do-host RTT. Jab tak wo nahi, defaults 'safe general' hi rahenge. Dhyan: kuch cheezein measure hi nahi hui (probe cost, per-process CPU), toh unke baare mein koi default decision data par nahi.
why_needed: Data ko default-badalne ya na-badalne ke faisle se jodna.
real_world_analogy: Doctor ki dose: report dekh ke bhi dose tabhi badalte hain jab report dose ke khilaf ho.
how_it_works: Evidence -> decision, aur 'koi badlav nahi' bhi ek valid decision hai.
in_this_project: README 'Defaults after measuring'; src/balancer.ts, src/proxy.ts defaults.
advantages: Kya badal sakta hai woh bhi likha
disadvantages: Production data nahi: defaults abhi bhi generic
common_mistakes: Data aane par bhi default badal dena chahe wo contradict na kare
Measurement ke bina defaults ko final bolna
follow_up_questions: CONNECT_TIMEOUT ko adaptive kaise banaoge?
Defaults ko environment ke profile (profiles) se kaise doge?

question: The proxy delivered about a quarter of the direct rate. How would you scale past one core, and what is NOT known?
answer_hinglish:
E1 ke hisaab se ek proxy process 3586 req/s par tha (shared 2-core machine, load generator aur upstream ke saath). Ek core ke aage badhne ke raaste: (1) ek hi machine par kai proxy processes (Node `cluster` ya alag ports par systemd instances) aur unke aage L4 distribution; (2) kai machines aur unke aage DNS ya cloud load balancer; (3) proxy ka kaam kam karna: logging band ya kam (4044 req/s mila, +12.8 percent), ya TLS Caddy par chhodna.

Kya NAHI pata: kai processes se scaling kitni milegi (maine multi-process measure nahi kiya), aur proxy sach mein ek core saturate kar raha tha ya nahi (per-process CPU measure nahi). 2 cores par load generator aur upstream bhi CPU le rahe the, toh proxy ke liye available CPU shayad ek core se kam tha. Isliye 'proxy ki limit 3586 req/s hai' kehna galat hoga: yeh us setup ki limit hai.

Aur multi-process ke saath nayi problems aati hain (PROXY-029, 058): per-process least-connections counters, per-process health state aur har process ka probe load. Interview mein pehle measure karne ki baat karo (per-process CPU, kya bottleneck hai), phir scaling. Kai baar bottleneck proxy nahi, upstream ya network hota hai.
why_needed: Scaling ke raaste jaante hue bhi unknowns ko naam se batana.
real_world_analogy: Ek counter par line lambi: pehle dekho cashier dheema hai ya system, phir counter badhao.
how_it_works: Single thread -> multiple processes ya machines; har process ka apna state.
advantages: Raaste aur unki nayi problems saaf
common_mistakes: Setup ki limit ko proxy ki limit bolna
Bina profile kiye scale karna
follow_up_questions: Node cluster kaise connections baanta hai?
CPU profile kaise lete hain (--cpu-prof)?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Zyada processes throughput badhate hain par state fragmentation (counters, health) aur probe load badhate hain. Pehle profile, phir scale.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Ek process ka crash baaki ko affect nahi karta par uski connections toot jaati hain; load balancer ko drain signal chahiye.
advanced.alternatives: nginx/Caddy ke native balancing, Go ya Rust proxy, L4 load balancer.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x: kai processes, L4 balancer. 100x: kai machines, DNS ya anycast.
advanced.production_improvements: Per-process CPU aur event-loop lag metrics, multi-process benchmark, aur shared ya sharded health.

question: How do you use the error field in the request log to understand a run?
answer_hinglish:
Har request ki log line mein ab `error` field hai: us request ke dauran dekhi gayi aakhri upstream error, jaise `ECONNREFUSED`, `ECONNRESET`, `ConnectTimeoutError`, `UpstreamTimeoutError`, ya `UPSTREAM_ABORTED` (body beech mein kati). Agar `attempts` 2 ya zyada hai aur status 200 hai, toh `error` woh failure hai jo retry ne client se chhupa li.

Soak mein is field se ek poori kahani padhi ja sakti hai: 2851253 requests mein sirf 26532 mein upstream error tha, aur sab ECONNRESET: flaky upstream ke 5 percent resets. 23819 requests retry hui (GET), aur client ne POST par 2713 502 dekhe (POST retry nahi hota). Yeh sab ek hi log se ginna ek chhoti script ka kaam hai.

Pehle yeh field nahi thi: 502 aata tha lekin reason nahi pata chalta tha (refused? reset? timeout?). Maine yeh gap pehle hi note kiya tha (PROXY-067) aur stage 4 se pehle fix kiya, kyunki E3, E4 aur E5 ki analysis isi par tiki hai. Limit: sirf aakhri error: agar ek request mein pehle ECONNREFUSED aur baad mein timeout aaye, toh sirf timeout dikhega.
why_needed: Logs se failures ko category mein gin sakna.
real_world_analogy: Rasid par sirf 'fail' likhne ke bajaye 'kyun fail' likhna.
how_it_works: Error code ya class ka naam `describeError` se aata hai aur log mein jaata hai.
in_this_project: src/proxy.ts::describeError, RequestLog.error; test/resilience.test.ts 'the log says why a request failed'.
code_example: jq -r 'select(.error) | .error' proxy.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
advantages: Failure reasons ginte ja sakte hain
Retry se chhupe failures bhi dikhte hain
disadvantages: Sirf aakhri error, saare attempts nahi
common_mistakes: Sirf status code dekhna
error field ko attempts ke bina padhna
follow_up_questions: Saare attempts ke errors kaise log karoge?
Is field se metric (counter) kaise banaoge?

question: What did deliberately breaking the code teach you across the whole project?
answer_hinglish:
Poore project mein maine 16 behaviours jaan-boojh ke tode (mid-response destroy, client-abort cancel, X-Forwarded-For trust, lease release, tie rule, retry policy, probe thresholds, ejection expiry, shutdown sweep, error log), aur har baar dekha ki matching test red hota hai. Zyadatar ek hi test ya do tests fail hue aur wapas restore karne par green.

Do asli gaps mile. (1) Body-less POST ka retry kisi test se nahi pakda gaya tha: method check hatane par bhi sab tests pass rahe, kyunki purana POST test body ke saath tha. Test add kiya. (2) Ek dead-port helper intermittent race wala tha (ek test ek baar fail hua, 25 dobara runs mein nahi): cause confirm nahi hua, par test files ab serial chalti hain. Aur ek apni galti: ek bar mere edit script ne ek file tod di aur maine broken commit kiya (push se pehle pakda, amend kiya): isse seekha ki commit ko 'pichle step success par hi' chain karo.

Seekh: green tests ka matlab 'kuch nahi toota', 'sab sahi hai' nahi. Mutation ke bina mujhe pata nahi chalta ki test sach mein kuch pakadta hai. Limit: yeh manual hai, toh sirf wahi behaviours todta hoon jo mujhe yaad aate hain. Ek automated tool (Stryker) zyada systematically karta. Aur har mutation ke baad restore aur full run zaroori.
why_needed: Test suite ki asli taqat ko parakhna.
real_world_analogy: Fire drill: sirf yeh dekhna ki alarm lagi hai kaafi nahi, bajake dekhna ki bajta hai.
how_it_works: Behaviour todo -> matching test red -> restore -> green. Gap mile toh test add karo.
in_this_project: test/ folder; README 'Checked by breaking the code' notes.
common_mistakes: Green tests ko correctness ka proof maan lena
Mutation ke baad restore bhoolna
follow_up_questions: Stryker jaise tools kaise kaam karte hain?
Mutation score ko CI mein kaise rakhoge?

question: What is a soak test, and why run one for 30 minutes?
answer_hinglish:
Soak test ka matlab hai system ko ek lambe samay tak (minutes se ghante) ek stable ya mixed load ke neeche chalana, taaki woh problems dikhein jo chhote tests mein nahi dikhti: memory ya connection leaks, counters ka drift, slow degradation, ya ek rare race jo kabhi kabhi hi hota hai. Chhota test (jaise 15 second ka benchmark) yeh sab miss kar deta hai kyunki leak dheere dheere badhta hai.

Is project mein soak E8 hai: 30 minute, 16 clients, random client aborts, POSTs, ek flaky upstream, aur active health checks. Maqsad capacity nahi tha: maqsad dekhna tha ki lagbhag 28 lakh requests ke baad kya system sahi state mein lauta (har active counter 0, memory plateau). Aur kuch rare events (health up/down, ECONNRESET) ho gaye jo chhote run mein shayad na hote.

30 minute kyun: compromise. Zyada lamba zyada bharosa deta hai par saari experiments ko ek ghante se zyada kheench deta. Iska matlab 30 minute 'proof' nahi: ek bahut dheemi leak nahi dikhegi. Production se pehle 24 ghante ka soak behtar hota. Soak ko chaos (random failures) ke saath chalana usse zyada realistic banata hai kyunki asli system mein bhi failures randomly aate hain.
why_needed: Long-running behaviour ko samajhna.
real_world_analogy: Naye phone ko ek hafte roz use karna: chhoti jaanch mein battery ya heating ki problem nahi dikhti.
how_it_works: Lambe samay tak load, phir state ke invariants (counters, memory) check.
code_example: SOAK_SECONDS=1800 node run.mjs e8 --label=a2-soak-30min
common_mistakes: Soak ko benchmark samajhna
Memory plateau ko 'no leak' maan lena
follow_up_questions: Soak ke dauran kya monitor karoge?
Heap snapshot kab lete hain?

question: What are p50, p97.5 and p99 latencies, and why report the median of several runs with a min-max?
answer_hinglish:
p50 (median) wo latency hai jisse 50 percent requests tez thi; p99 se 99 percent tez thi, yani sabse dheemi 1 percent us se zyada. Average akela bhramak hota hai kyunki kuch bahut dheemi requests use kheench deti hain; percentiles tail dikhate hain, jo users ko asli mein chubhta hai. Is project mein E1 mein direct ka p99 4 ms tha aur proxy ka 14 ms.

E2 ka sabak: least-connections ne median 15 se 6 ms kiya, lekin p99 46 se 49 ms (behtar nahi hua). Agar sirf average ya median dekhte toh tail ki baat chhoot jaati.

Median of 3 runs aur min-max kyun: ek run kisi bhi wajah se (noisy neighbour, GC pause) off ho sakta hai. Median us outlier ko nakar deta hai, aur min-max dikhata hai ki run ek doosre se kitne alag the (E1 mein proxy ka min-max 3251 - 3608). Agar spread bada ho toh nateeje par bharosa kam. 3 runs bahut kam hain statistical confidence ke liye; yeh ek practical compromise hai. Aur autocannon ke percentiles ek histogram se bante hain, exact nahi.
why_needed: Latency numbers ko sahi padhna.
real_world_analogy: Roz ke office ke safar mein 'aksar 30 minute' (median) aur 'har 100 mein ek din 2 ghante' (p99) alag batein batate hain.
how_it_works: Sorted latencies mein percentile position. Median of runs outlier ko dabata hai.
code_example: const trim = (r) => ({ rps: r.requests.average, p50: r.latency.p50, p97_5: r.latency.p97_5, p99: r.latency.p99 /* ... */ });
common_mistakes: Sirf average dekhna
Ek run ka best number batana
follow_up_questions: Coordinated omission kya hota hai?
p99.9 kab zaroori hota hai?

question: What is honestly still unfinished in H11, and what would you do next?
answer_hinglish:
Jo ho chuka hai: proxy, load balancing, health checks, retries, connect timeout, ek asli server par measured results (single host), ek shutdown defect fix, aur systemd service ready. Jo NAHI hua aur isliye kisi ko claim nahi karna chahiye: (1) do-host mode: asli network RTT, EHOSTUNREACH, poori machine ka failover; (2) public URL: Caddy aur DuckDNS ke saath koi bhi bahar se isse nahi chala sakta, aur iska koi measurement nahi; (3) upload ki memory, kai bade transfers ek saath, per-process CPU, probe cost; (4) production error rates ya capacity.

Features jo nahi hain: weights, sticky sessions, draining, runtime config reload, panic mode, success-rate ejection, retry budget aur backoff, slow start, WebSocket, HTTPS upstream. Service ki security score 5.8 MEDIUM hai: aur hardening mumkin.

Agla kadam (priority order): (a) retry budget aur backoff: sasta, aur retry storm ka risk band karta hai; (b) success-rate ejection ke saath max ejection percent: partial failures aur cascading ejection dono ko sambhalta; (c) draining aur slow start: deploys ke liye; (d) do-host measurement, tabhi jab ek reversible, chhota network rule theek lage. Interview mein yeh list saaf batana ('yeh banaya, yeh measure kiya, yeh chhoda') bahut zyada bharosa deta hai.
why_needed: Project ki honest sthiti batana senior engineering ka hissa hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar bana: neev, deewaren aur chhat taiyar; plastering aur furniture baaki: dono saaf batana.
how_it_works: Done, measured, not done: teen alag bucket.
common_mistakes: Claim ko 'production-ready' kehna
Not-done list ko chhupana
follow_up_questions: Retry budget kaise implement karoge?
Production-ready ke liye minimum checklist kya hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Zyada features ke bajaye pehle chhote reliability gaps (budget, draining) bharna behtar; features baad mein.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Retry storm bina budget ke; cascading ejection bina max ejection limit ke; deploy mein dropped requests bina draining ke.
advanced.alternatives: Caddy ya nginx ke built-in features ko hi use karna aur apna proxy seekhne ke liye rakhna.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x par budget aur draining must; 100x par control plane aur shared health.
advanced.production_improvements: Retry budget, success-rate ejection, draining, slow start, metrics, aur do-host load test.
